commitResults.messageTitle: added banner
added level1-echo
added level2-add,list
Task: Add completion status commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks do not retain a completion state or support status changes.

Introduce a Task model with done status and use it for task storage.

Display status icons in list output.

Support mark and unmark commands so users can track task completion.

commitResults.messageTitle: Task types: Add todos, deadlines, and events
commitResults.messageBody:
The task list supports only generic tasks and cannot retain date or time details.

Add Todo, Deadline, and Event subclasses and parse their commands into the shared Task array. Keep date and time values as strings until the later date-handling increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Errors: Handle invalid commands safely
commitResults.messageBody:
Invalid commands can crash the chatbot or produce unclear feedback.

Raise BaemaxException for malformed task commands, invalid task numbers, blank input, and unknown commands.

Show friendly Baemax-specific messages while keeping valid commands running.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tasks: Add deletion and collection storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need to remove obsolete tasks without restarting Baemax.

Store tasks in an ArrayList so deletion shifts remaining tasks safely and the list can grow dynamically.

Validate delete task numbers with the existing exception-based command handling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Persist tasks to a save file
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks live only in memory, so the whole list is lost when the
chatbot exits.

Let's add a Storage class that writes every task to
./data/baemax.txt whenever the list changes, creating the data
folder on first use. Each task encodes itself through a new
toFileFormat method, composed via super calls in the same way as
toString.

Reading the file back on startup will follow in a later commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Load saved tasks on startup
commitResults.messageBody:
The save file is written but never read, so a restart still begins
with an empty list.

Let's have Storage.load parse the file into Task objects and have
Baemax seed the list with them before the greeting. A missing file
or data folder yields an empty list, which is the expected state
the first time the chatbot runs on a new computer. Lines that do
not match the expected format are skipped with a warning so a
single bad line does not drop the rest of the list.

Ignore the runtime-generated /data/ folder so a user's own tasks
are not committed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
Deadline: Store the due date as a LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
A deadline keeps its due date as a plain String, so the chatbot
cannot reason about it and shows it back exactly as typed.

Let's parse the /by text into a java.time.LocalDate. A new Dates
helper holds the single input format (yyyy-MM-dd) and display
format (MMM dd yyyy) used across the app; text that is not a valid
date raises a BaemaxException with guidance. The save file keeps
the ISO yyyy-MM-dd form, which LocalDate reads back directly, and
an unreadable date now falls into Storage's skip-bad-line path.

commitResults.messageTitle: Event: Store the start and end as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
An event keeps its start and end as plain Strings, matching the
old Deadline design that has since moved to LocalDate.

Let's parse the /from and /to text into java.time.LocalDate via
the shared Dates helper, so events accept and display dates the
same way deadlines do. Command hints and the save/load path are
updated to match; unreadable dates are skipped on load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-8'
Ui: Extract user interaction into its own class
commitResults.messageBody:
Baemax mixes command handling with the details of talking to the
user: it builds the banner, prints dividers, reads from a Scanner,
and calls System.out.println throughout its helper methods. This
makes the main class harder to read and would make it hard to
swap the console for another front end later.

Let's move every read from System.in and write to System.out into
a new Ui class (showWelcome, showGoodbye, showLine, readCommand,
hasNextCommand, show, showError, close). Baemax now holds a Ui
instance and delegates all interaction to it, leaving its methods
focused on what each command does.

This is the first step of A-MoreOOP. Behaviour is unchanged; the
one visible difference is that a corrupted-save-file warning now
prints just after the greeting rather than between the banner and
the greeting, since the banner and greeting are emitted together.

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Extract the task collection into its own class
commitResults.messageBody:
Baemax holds a raw ArrayList<Task> and every command helper pokes
at it directly with index arithmetic, so the list mechanics are
spread across the main class.

Let's move the collection and its operations into a TaskList class
(add, remove, get, size, asList), with remove and get taking the
one-based number the user typed. Baemax now keeps a TaskList and
asks it for tasks instead of managing a list itself; Storage still
saves a plain List via asList(). This is the class the A-MoreOOP
target constructs as new TaskList(storage.load()).

Behaviour is unchanged (verified against the command scenario).

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Extract command interpretation into its own class
commitResults.messageBody:
Baemax both drives the chatbot loop and knows the grammar of every
command: how a todo/deadline/event is written and how a task
number is read from a mark/unmark/delete command.

Let's move that parsing into a Parser class. parseTask builds a
Task from an add command; parseTaskNumber reads and range-checks
the task number, taking the current task count as an argument
rather than reaching for the list. Baemax now calls Parser and is
left with dispatch and response logic.

Behaviour is unchanged (verified against the command scenario).

commitResults.messageTitle: Baemax: Turn the entry point into an object with run()
commitResults.messageBody:
Baemax holds its collaborators as static fields and does its work
in a static main plus static helpers, so the whole chatbot is one
implicit global object.

Let's give Baemax a constructor that takes the save-file path and
wires up Ui, Storage, and TaskList, a run() method for the command
loop, and a one-line main that does new Baemax(path).run(). All
helpers become instance methods. This matches the structure the
A-MoreOOP brief suggests.

Tasks are now loaded in the constructor rather than after the
greeting; happy-path output is unchanged (verified against the
command scenario), and a corrupted-save-file warning would now
appear just before the banner.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-MoreOOP'
All: Put every class in the baemax package
commitResults.messageBody:
Every class sits in the default package, which is discouraged for
anything beyond a toy program and leaves no room to group related
classes.

Let's move all classes under src/main/java/baemax and declare
package baemax in each. src/main/java stays the source root, so
Gradle and other tools still find the sources. The main class is
now baemax.Baemax; the README run step and its sample output are
updated to match.

This is the minimal form of A-Packages (one package). A finer
split such as baemax.task can come later as the class count grows.
Behaviour is unchanged (verified against the command scenario).

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Packages'
Merge branch 'add-gradle-support'
Gradle: Point the build at baemax.Baemax
commitResults.messageBody:
The build script merged from add-gradle-support still names the
template's main class, seedu.duke.Duke, so `gradle run` and the
generated launch scripts fail to start the app.

Let's set application.mainClass to baemax.Baemax and name the
shadowJar output baemax.jar to match this project. `./gradlew
build` and `./gradlew run` now work; run output matches the
pre-Gradle behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test: Add JUnit tests for Dates, Parser, and TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
The project has no automated tests, so every check of the parsing
and list logic is done by hand through the UI.

Let's add JUnit 5 tests under src/test/java/baemax for the classes
with the most branching:
- DatesTest: yyyy-MM-dd parsing (valid, whitespace, wrong format,
  out-of-range month, trailing text, empty) and MMM dd yyyy
  formatting, including a round trip.
- ParserTest: parseTask for todo/deadline/event happy paths and
  every malformed-command branch, plus parseTaskNumber for range
  and syntax errors.
- TaskListTest: one-based add/get/remove, size, seeding from an
  external list, and out-of-range access.

35 tests, run with ./gradlew test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-JUnit'
Style: Tighten visibility and drop redundant code
commitResults.messageBody:
Parts of the code do not follow the SE-EDU Java coding standard:
task fields are protected without any subclass needing them, the
utility classes Dates and Parser can be instantiated, and
getStatusIcon wraps a return value in parentheses with a comment
that just restates the code.

Let's make Task, Deadline, and Event fields private (and final
where they never change), give Dates and Parser private
constructors so they cannot be instantiated, and simplify
getStatusIcon. Two private helpers in Baemax also gain the
@param/@throws tags the rest of the class already uses.

No behaviour change; tests and the command scenario still pass,
and `javadoc` now reports no warnings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Add a command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can only see tasks via the full list, so locating one task
in a long list means scanning it by eye.

Let's add a find <keyword> command that shows the tasks whose
description contains the keyword (case-insensitive), numbered from
one. TaskList.find does the filtering, Task.getDescription exposes
the text to match against, and Baemax.findTasks handles the
command and rejects an empty keyword. The "unknown command" hints
now mention find too.

This is Level-9. New JUnit tests cover TaskList.find; the command
scenario still passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-CodingStandard'
Merge branch 'branch-Level-9'
commitResults.messageBody:
Resolve a conflict in Baemax.java: keep the new findTasks method
from branch-Level-9 alongside the expanded addTask Javadoc from
branch-A-CodingStandard.

commitResults.messageTitle: Dates: Accept flexible date and time input
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines and events only accept a due date in strict yyyy-MM-dd
form and cannot carry a time of day, so natural input like
"4/9/2026 1600" is rejected.

Let's replace the Dates helper with a TaskDate value type that
holds a date plus an optional time. TaskDate.parse accepts
yyyy-MM-dd, d/M/yyyy, d-M-yyyy, "d MMM yyyy" and "MMM d yyyy",
each optionally followed by a time such as 1800, 18:00, 6pm, or
6:30pm; month names are case-insensitive. Deadline and Event now
hold TaskDate instead of LocalDate.

The save file keeps ISO form: "2026-09-04" for a date,
"2026-09-04T16:00" when a time is set, both read back by
TaskDate.fromStorage. Existing date-only save files still load
unchanged. Display adds ", h:mma" only when a time is present.

DatesTest is replaced by TaskDateTest; 44 tests pass and javadoc
is warning-free.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-flexible-datetime'
Checkstyle: Add automated coding-standard checks
commitResults.messageBody:
The coding standard is only checked by eye, so a stray tab, an
unsorted import, or a missing Javadoc could slip in unnoticed.

Let's add the Gradle checkstyle plugin with the SE-EDU config
(config/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml plus suppressions.xml, taken
from AddressBook Level 3), which encodes the same standard the
project already follows. checkstyleMain and checkstyleTest now run
as part of `gradlew build`.

No code changes were needed: `gradlew checkstyleMain
checkstyleTest` reports zero violations across all 14 source
files, since A-CodingStandard already brought the code into line.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-CheckStyle'
Baemax: Return command responses as strings
commitResults.messageBody:
Command handlers print directly through Ui, so a GUI front end
cannot reuse them: it needs the reply as a value, not console
output.

Let's have processCommand and each handler return their response
text, and add a public getResponse(String) that turns one line of
input into one reply (handling bye and BaemaxException). run() now
frames that reply with the console divider, so command-line output
is unchanged. Ui loses the now-unused showGoodbye and showError,
and showWelcome is split into showBanner plus a getWelcomeMessage
on Baemax that both front ends can use.

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Add a JavaFX front end
commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot only runs as a console app.

Let's add a JavaFX GUI beside it: Launcher (entry point that works
around the JavaFX classpath issue), Main (loads the window and
injects a Baemax), MainWindow (controller that turns typed input
into a getResponse call and shows both sides as dialog boxes), and
DialogBox (one chat bubble, avatar flipped to the left for
Baemax's replies). Layouts live in MainWindow.fxml and
DialogBox.fxml; the two avatars are placeholder images.

build.gradle gains the JavaFX dependencies (stock configuration
from the SE-EDU tutorial) and points application.mainClass at
Launcher, so `gradlew run` and the jar start the GUI. The console
UI stays available via Baemax.main. New BaemaxTest covers the
getResponse reply path; 49 tests pass and checkstyle is clean.

The bye command still works: the GUI shows the farewell, then
closes itself after a short pause.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-10'
GUI: Clip avatars to a circle
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Circle clip to the DialogBox ImageView so the square avatar
images render as circles.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: Drop the sparkle from the greeting
Baemax: Use varargs to build multi-line responses
commitResults.messageBody:
The confirmation messages for add, delete, mark, and unmark glue
two or three lines together with embedded "\n", which is easy to
misread.

Let's add a small lines(String...) helper that joins its
arguments with newlines, and have those handlers pass their lines
as separate arguments. Ui.show(String...) already uses varargs in
the same spirit. Output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Varargs'
GUI: Add a matcha-green theme and a pixel font
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI uses the default JavaFX look, which feels generic.

Let's add a sage/matcha colour scheme via a stylesheet
(view/style.css): pale-green window, rounded chat bubbles in two
shades for the user and Baemax, and a matcha Send button. Bundle
the VT323 pixel font (SIL OFL, license included) and set it as the
app font. DialogBox tags itself with style classes so the reply
bubbles can be coloured differently.
